formulas.title: Taxable-income pipeline
formulas.formula: Gross income − above-line deductions = AGI; AGI − applicable below-line deductions = taxable income
formulas.meaning: Gross income inclusions/exclusions are determined first. Above-line amounts depend on §62; below-line amounts depend on §63 and other rules.
formulas.worked: Start with wages, business gross profit and other included receipts, then identify permitted adjustments and the larger applicable standard/itemized deduction.

formulas.title: Gross profit from inventory
formulas.formula: Gross profit = sales receipts − cost of goods sold
formulas.meaning: COGS is recovered in measuring gross income from inventory sales.
formulas.worked: Textbook: 2 hammers × $20 = $40 gross receipts; 2 × $12 = $24 COGS; $16 gross profit.

formulas.title: Deduction tax saving
formulas.formula: Approximate tax saving = usable deduction × marginal tax rate
formulas.meaning: This shortcut assumes deduction is fully allowed and does not cross brackets or affect phaseouts.
formulas.worked: Textbook: a $50 incremental itemized deduction at 33% marginal rate saves $16.50.

formulas.title: Tax credit offset
formulas.formula: Tax after nonrefundable credit = max(0, preliminary tax − usable credit)
formulas.meaning: Refundable credits can exceed liability and generate a refund; nonrefundable credits generally cannot.
formulas.worked: Textbook contrasts a $100 credit against a $100 deduction.

formulas.title: Average tax rate
formulas.formula: Average tax rate = tax liability ÷ specified measure of income
formulas.meaning: Specify taxable income versus economic income; negative liabilities possible with refundable credits.
formulas.worked: Textbook hypothetical: $14,000 tax / $60,000 taxable income = 23.33% average rate.

formulas.title: Layered marginal bracket
formulas.formula: Total tax = Σ (income in each bracket × its rate)
formulas.meaning: A higher bracket applies only to the slice of taxable income falling in it.

formulas.title: After-tax marginal earnings
formulas.formula: After-tax extra earnings ≈ extra pay × (1 − marginal rate)
formulas.meaning: Assumes extra amount remains within relevant bracket and excludes other taxes/phaseouts.
formulas.worked: Textbook hypothetical: $10,000 × (1 − 25%) = $7,500.

formulas.title: Tax gross-up of charitable cost
formulas.formula: Net cash cost of usable deduction ≈ gift − gift × marginal rate
formulas.meaning: Only applies when deductible and incrementally useful.
formulas.worked: Textbook compares $1,000 gifts at 15% versus 30% rates.

formulas.title: Adjusted basis
formulas.formula: Adjusted basis = initial basis + capital improvements − prior basis reductions
formulas.meaning: General conceptual expression; include depreciation and other adjustments under the Code.
formulas.worked: A capital asset is not necessarily deductible when bought; basis matters for future cost recovery.

formulas.title: Realized gain or loss
formulas.formula: Realized gain/loss = amount realized − adjusted basis
formulas.meaning: Recognition of realized gain may be delayed or excluded under a separate statute.
formulas.worked: Textbook illustration: land worth $5m with $1m basis exchanged for property worth $5m → $4m realized gain; §1031 may defer if requirements met.

formulas.title: Simple nominal versus real gain
formulas.formula: Nominal gain = proceeds − historical basis; real purchasing-power gain adjusts for inflation
formulas.meaning: Tax law does not generally inflation-adjust investment basis.
formulas.worked: Textbook: buy at $100, sell at $105 after 5% inflation → $5 nominal gain but ~0 real gain.

formulas.title: Compound future value
formulas.formula: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n
formulas.meaning: PV initial investment; r return per period; n number of periods.

formulas.title: Present value
formulas.formula: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)^n
formulas.meaning: Discount rate r and number of periods n must match.
formulas.worked: Textbook Table 1-5: 10 years at 10% ≈ .386 multiplier; $10,000 in 10 years ≈ $3,855.43 today (table rounds to $3,860).

formulas.title: Deferral versus current taxation
formulas.formula: Deferral: P(1+r)^n(1−t_end); current tax: P(1−t_now)[1+r(1−t_annual)]^n
formulas.meaning: The source assumes constant tax rates, ordinary annual taxation of earnings, and equal pre-tax returns.
formulas.worked: 10 years: $10,000 deferred at 10%, 40% retirement tax ≈ $15,562; current 40% tax plus annual after-tax 6% ≈ $10,745.

formulas.title: Penalty percentages (introductory)
formulas.formula: Illustrative accuracy-related penalty = 20% × relevant underpayment; civil fraud = 75% × fraudulent portion
formulas.meaning: Penalties require legal predicates, bases, exceptions, and interaction rules; do not use formula alone.
formulas.worked: Textbook introduces these percentages in its compliance overview.

formulas.title: Refund / balance due
formulas.formula: Tax due after credits − withholding/estimated payments = remaining balance (if positive) or refund (if negative)
formulas.meaning: Eligibility, refundable credits, additional taxes, and payment credit details must be included in a full return.
formulas.worked: Self-assessment and prepayments are reconciled when filing the annual return.

formulas.title: Haig–Simons income
formulas.formula: Y = C + ΔW (consumption + change in wealth)
formulas.meaning: Economic definition of personal income, distinct from statutory taxable income.
formulas.worked: C=$11,000, net worth changes by −$1,000, so Y=$10,000. Borrowing $1,000 finances the excess consumption, not additional economic income.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 37–38

formulas.title: Income as consumption plus saving
formulas.formula: Y = C + S
formulas.meaning: An alternate shorthand when saving measures the period's change in net worth.
formulas.worked: If spending $9,000 and adding $1,000 to savings, income is $10,000.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 37

formulas.title: Valuation of noncash remuneration
formulas.formula: Generally include FMV of property or services received for services rendered
formulas.meaning: Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1) generally measures in-kind compensation by FMV.
formulas.worked: A carpenter provides renovations to a lawyer in exchange for a will: identify the fair market value of what was exchanged and any matching consequences.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 46

formulas.title: Gain and per-share basis allocation
formulas.formula: Allocated basis = acquisition cost × (shares sold ÷ shares acquired); gain = proceeds − allocated basis
formulas.meaning: Useful for identical shares originally acquired as one block.
formulas.worked: Purchase 100 shares for $1,000. Sell 40 for $700. Basis = $400; realized gain = $300.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 68

formulas.title: Relative-value allocation of land basis
formulas.formula: Allocated basis = total basis × (relative FMV of portion at acquisition ÷ total FMV at acquisition)
formulas.meaning: Where land portions differ in value, allocate tax basis reasonably rather than by area alone.
formulas.worked: Whole land cost $1,000; wooded part represents 45% of total original value. Basis of wooded land $450. Sell for $700 → $250 gain.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 68–69

formulas.title: Inaja basis-reduction illustration
formulas.formula: Remaining basis = initial basis − payment treated as return of capital
formulas.meaning: Used only when legally appropriate and apportionment to disposed rights is impracticable.
formulas.worked: Inaja: property original cost $61,000; net settlement $49,000 treated as capital recovery. Remaining basis conceptually $12,000, absent other adjustments.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 69–70

formulas.title: 2026 wagering loss limitation
formulas.formula: Allowable loss deduction = min(90% × wagering losses, wagering gains)
formulas.meaning: The §165(d) tax-year-2026 statutory change supersedes the textbook's earlier full-offset example.
formulas.worked: If wagering gains total $1,000 and losses $1,000, the statutory limit permits at most $900 loss deduction in 2026, subject to individual itemizing/other applicable rules.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 71–73 + 2026 current law

formulas.title: Compensation for damaged business property
formulas.formula: Potential realized gain = recovery proceeds − adjusted basis (before §1033 relief)
formulas.meaning: Consider property basis and qualifying nonrecognition for reinvestment.
formulas.worked: Destroyed building with adjusted basis $600,000; insurance recovery $700,000. Potential $100,000 gain absent §1033 nonrecognition.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 78

formulas.title: §107 minister housing allowance limits
formulas.formula: Excludable housing allowance = min(designated allowance, actual qualifying housing expenses, fair rental value including furnishings/utilities)
formulas.meaning: IRS conditions and current statutory limits apply; distinguish from self-employment tax treatment.
formulas.worked: If designated $30,000, actual housing costs $28,000, and FMV cap $25,000, the income-tax exclusion generally cannot exceed $25,000, subject to all qualifications.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. Gaylor PDF; IRC §107 and IRS guidance

formulas.title: Principal residence sale gain
formulas.formula: Potential taxable gain = max(0, realized gain − permissible §121 exclusion)
formulas.meaning: After computing gain, determine use/ownership tests, $250,000/$500,000 cap, and frequency limitations.
formulas.worked: Basis $100,000; sale proceeds $400,000; gain $300,000. If a single filer qualifies for $250,000 exclusion, taxable gain $50,000.
formulas.source: Bankman et al., Federal Income Taxation (19th ed.), Chapter 2, p. 100–101
